exercises.title: Asset directory
exercises.prompt: List the OBJ_CODE and OBJ_DESC of every R5OBJECTS record.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_CODE,
       OBJ_DESC
FROM R5OBJECTS WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A'
exercises.reason: Name only the columns a reader needs; each R5OBJECTS row describes one asset.

exercises.title: Where work happens
exercises.prompt: List the distinct OBJ_LOCATION names in R5OBJECTS.
exercises.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT OBJ_LOCATION
FROM R5OBJECTS WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A'
exercises.reason: DISTINCT collapses repeated output values after selecting the location.

exercises.title: Open work
exercises.prompt: Return EVT_CODE and EVT_OBJECT for open work orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVT_CODE,
       EVT_OBJECT
FROM R5EVENTS
WHERE EVT_STATUS='Open'
exercises.reason: WHERE tests each order before it appears in the result.

exercises.title: High priority in Utilities
exercises.prompt: Return asset codes that are both High OBJ_CRITICALITY and in Utilities.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_CODE
FROM R5OBJECTS
WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A' AND OBJ_CRITICALITY='High'
  AND OBJ_LOCATION='Utilities'
exercises.reason: Combine both tests with AND so an asset must satisfy each condition.

exercises.title: Two status bands
exercises.prompt: List codes for assets whose OBJ_CRITICALITY is either High or Medium.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_CODE
FROM R5OBJECTS
WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A' AND OBJ_CRITICALITY IN ('High',
                      'Medium')
exercises.reason: IN expresses a choice between a small set of allowed values.

exercises.title: Midrange costs
exercises.prompt: Return order ID and cost for orders costing 300 through 600 inclusive.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVO_EVENT,
       EVO_TOTAL
FROM R5EVENTCOST
WHERE EVO_TOTAL BETWEEN 300 AND 600
exercises.reason: BETWEEN includes both boundary amounts.

exercises.title: Pump codes
exercises.prompt: List R5OBJECTS codes beginning with PUMP. Match the prefix regardless of suffix.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_CODE
FROM R5OBJECTS
WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A' AND OBJ_CODE LIKE 'PUMP%'
exercises.reason: The trailing wildcard permits any remaining characters after the prefix.

exercises.title: Outside Production
exercises.prompt: Return OBJ_CODE and OBJ_LOCATION for assets outside Production.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_CODE,
       OBJ_LOCATION
FROM R5OBJECTS
WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A' AND OBJ_LOCATION <> 'Production'
exercises.reason: Use an inequality comparison on location.

exercises.title: Two costliest orders
exercises.prompt: List the two highest-cost orders as EVO_EVENT and cost. Break ties with smaller IDs first. Preserve this order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVO_EVENT,
       EVO_TOTAL
FROM R5EVENTCOST
ORDER BY EVO_TOTAL DESC,
         EVO_EVENT
LIMIT 2
exercises.reason: Sort before limiting. The ID tie-breaker makes the selection repeatable.

exercises.title: Count the backlog
exercises.prompt: Return a single count of open work orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM R5EVENTS
WHERE EVT_STATUS='Open'
exercises.reason: Filter to the backlog before counting the remaining rows.

exercises.title: Total booked hours
exercises.prompt: Return total BOO_HOURS from all R5BOOKEDHOURS.
exercises.sql:
SELECT SUM(BOO_HOURS)
FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS
exercises.reason: SUM adds the values across all bookings.

exercises.title: Typical order cost
exercises.prompt: Return average work-order cost rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(EVO_TOTAL), 2)
FROM R5EVENTCOST
exercises.reason: Round the aggregate once to avoid intermediate rounding errors.

exercises.title: Cost extremes
exercises.prompt: Return one row with the minimum and maximum work-order cost, in that order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT MIN(EVO_TOTAL),
       MAX(EVO_TOTAL)
FROM R5EVENTCOST
exercises.reason: Two aggregates without grouping describe the same whole set.

exercises.title: Issue line value
exercises.prompt: For every material issue return ID and extended value: quantity times ISS_PRICE.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ISS_PK,
       ISS_QTY*ISS_PRICE
FROM R5ISSUES
exercises.reason: Multiplication is evaluated separately on each issue line.

exercises.title: Reorder gap
exercises.prompt: For R5STOCK below its reorder level, return part, store and units short.
exercises.sql:
SELECT STO_PART,
       STO_STORE,
       STO_ORDLEV-STO_QTY
FROM R5STOCK
WHERE STO_QTY<STO_ORDLEV
exercises.reason: Apply the threshold at part-store level before calculating the positive gap.

exercises.title: Case-normalized identifiers
exercises.prompt: Return each supplier COM_CODE and its lowercase form.
exercises.sql:
SELECT COM_CODE,
       LOWER(COM_CODE)
FROM R5COMPANIES
exercises.reason: LOWER transforms the output while retaining the original identifier for comparison.

exercises.title: Description length
exercises.prompt: Return each asset OBJ_CODE and the number of characters in its description.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_CODE,
       LENGTH(OBJ_DESC)
FROM R5OBJECTS WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A'
exercises.reason: LENGTH counts text characters in SQLite.

exercises.title: Month label
exercises.prompt: For every meter reading, return REA_CODE and its YYYY-MM month.
exercises.sql:
SELECT REA_CODE,
       SUBSTR(REA_DATE, 1, 7)
FROM R5READINGS
exercises.reason: The ISO date starts with a four-digit year, a hyphen and a two-digit month.

exercises.title: Missing reviewer
exercises.prompt: List event IDs in R5AUDVALUES whose AVA_MODIFIEDBY is NULL.
exercises.sql:
SELECT AVA_SQLIDENTITY
FROM R5AUDVALUES
WHERE AVA_MODIFIEDBY IS NULL
exercises.reason: Test absence with IS NULL. Equality to NULL does not produce a true condition.

exercises.title: Reviewer fallback
exercises.prompt: For every order event return AVA_SQLIDENTITY and AVA_MODIFIEDBY, displaying Unassigned when AVA_MODIFIEDBY is NULL.
exercises.sql:
SELECT AVA_SQLIDENTITY,
       COALESCE(AVA_MODIFIEDBY, 'Unassigned')
FROM R5AUDVALUES
exercises.reason: COALESCE selects its first non-null argument.

exercises.title: Cost bands
exercises.prompt: Return EVO_EVENT and the label Large for orders costing at least 500, otherwise Standard.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVO_EVENT,
       CASE
           WHEN EVO_TOTAL>=500 THEN 'Large'
           ELSE 'Standard'
       END
FROM R5EVENTCOST
exercises.reason: CASE maps a numeric rule to a readable category.

exercises.title: Receipt chronology
exercises.prompt: Return receipt DKL_DCKCODE, DKL_ORDER and DKL_RECVQTY with the newest ID first. Preserve this order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT DKL_DCKCODE,
       DKL_ORDER,
       DKL_RECVQTY
FROM R5DOCKLINES
ORDER BY DKL_DCKCODE DESC
exercises.reason: A descending key traverses the imported receipt IDs from largest to smallest.

exercises.title: Distinct assets with work
exercises.prompt: Return the number of different R5OBJECTS codes appearing in work orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT EVT_OBJECT)
FROM R5EVENTS
exercises.reason: Counting distinct R5OBJECTS answers a different question from counting orders.

exercises.title: Inspection outcomes
exercises.prompt: Return result and number of R5ACTCHECKLISTS for each result value.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ACK_FINDING,
       COUNT(*)
FROM R5ACTCHECKLISTS
GROUP BY ACK_FINDING
exercises.reason: Grouping changes the output from one row per inspection to one per outcome.

exercises.title: Parts used twice
exercises.prompt: List part and total issued ISS_QTY for R5PARTS whose combined issued ISS_QTY is at least two.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ISS_PART,
       SUM(ISS_QTY)
FROM R5ISSUES
GROUP BY ISS_PART
HAVING SUM(ISS_QTY)>=2
exercises.reason: HAVING filters totals after each part group is formed.

exercises.title: Name the equipment
exercises.prompt: For each work order return order id, R5OBJECTS description and status.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.EVT_CODE,
       e.OBJ_DESC,
       w.EVT_STATUS
FROM R5EVENTS w
JOIN R5OBJECTS e ON e.OBJ_CODE=w.EVT_OBJECT WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A'
exercises.reason: Attach the R5OBJECTS description using the asset primary key.

exercises.title: Find the employer organization
exercises.prompt: For each department return department code and owning organization name.
exercises.sql:
SELECT d.MRC_CODE,
       o.ORG_DESC
FROM R5MRCS d
JOIN R5ORGANIZATION o ON o.ORG_CODE=d.MRC_ORG
exercises.reason: The organization code is the link from a department to its single owner.

exercises.title: Bookings by trade
exercises.prompt: Return trade and total booked hours grouped by the employee’s assigned trade.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.PER_TRADE,
       SUM(l.BOO_HOURS)
FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS l
JOIN R5PERSONNEL e ON e.PER_CODE=l.BOO_PERSON
GROUP BY e.PER_TRADE
exercises.reason: Join the employee for classification, then aggregate the booking rows.

exercises.title: Supplier spend
exercises.prompt: For R5COMPANIES with purchase lines, return supplier code and total ordered value.
exercises.sql:
SELECT p.ORD_SUPPLIER,
       SUM(l.ORL_ORDQTY*l.ORL_PRICE)
FROM R5ORDERS p
JOIN R5ORDERLINES l ON l.ORL_ORDER=p.ORD_CODE
GROUP BY p.ORD_SUPPLIER
exercises.reason: Calculate value at line level before rolling it up to supplier.

exercises.title: Include idle assets
exercises.prompt: Return every asset code and its count of work orders, including zero.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.OBJ_CODE,
       COUNT(w.EVT_CODE)
FROM R5OBJECTS e
LEFT JOIN R5EVENTS w ON w.EVT_OBJECT=e.OBJ_CODE
WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A' GROUP BY e.OBJ_CODE
exercises.reason: Count a matched order ID so the preserved empty asset contributes zero.

exercises.title: Uninspected equipment
exercises.prompt: Return codes of assets with no inspection record.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.OBJ_CODE
FROM R5OBJECTS e
WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A' AND NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM R5ACTCHECKLISTS i
     WHERE i.ACK_OBJECT=e.OBJ_CODE)
exercises.reason: An anti-join keeps an asset when the correlated lookup finds no inspection.

exercises.title: Orders with materials
exercises.prompt: Return IDs of work orders with at least one material issue, once per order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.EVT_CODE
FROM R5EVENTS w
WHERE EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM R5ISSUES m
     WHERE m.ISS_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE)
exercises.reason: EXISTS tests membership without multiplying an order by its issue count.

exercises.title: Above the mean
exercises.prompt: Return EVO_EVENT and cost for orders costing strictly more than the overall order average.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVO_EVENT,
       EVO_TOTAL
FROM R5EVENTCOST
WHERE EVO_TOTAL>
    (SELECT AVG(EVO_TOTAL)
     FROM R5EVENTCOST)
exercises.reason: A scalar subquery supplies one threshold to every outer row.

exercises.title: Store totals
exercises.prompt: Return store, total on-hand units and distinct stocked part count per store.
exercises.sql:
SELECT STO_STORE,
       SUM(STO_QTY),
       COUNT(DISTINCT STO_PART)
FROM R5STOCK
GROUP BY STO_STORE
exercises.reason: The two aggregates measure volume and assortment separately.

exercises.title: Open and closed counts
exercises.prompt: For every R5OBJECTS code present in R5EVENTS return code, open count and closed count.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVT_OBJECT,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN EVT_STATUS='Open' THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END),
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN EVT_STATUS='Closed' THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END)
FROM R5EVENTS
GROUP BY EVT_OBJECT
exercises.reason: Conditional sums create status columns without filtering away other rows.

exercises.title: Line receipt balance
exercises.prompt: For every purchase line return DKL_ORDER, line and ordered quantity less cumulative R5DOCKLINES. Include unreceived lines.
exercises.sql:
SELECT l.ORL_ORDER,
       l.ORL_ORDLINE,
       l.ORL_ORDQTY-COALESCE(SUM(r.DKL_RECVQTY), 0)
FROM R5ORDERLINES l
LEFT JOIN R5DOCKLINES r ON r.DKL_ORDER=l.ORL_ORDER
AND r.DKL_ORDLINE=l.ORL_ORDLINE
GROUP BY l.ORL_ORDER,
         l.ORL_ORDLINE,
         l.ORL_ORDQTY
exercises.reason: Use the two-part line identity; an absent receipt contributes zero.

exercises.title: Monthly reading count
exercises.prompt: Return meter, YYYY-MM and count of readings for each observed meter-month.
exercises.sql:
SELECT REA_METER,
       strftime('%Y-%m', REA_DATE),
       COUNT(*)
FROM R5READINGS
GROUP BY REA_METER,
         strftime('%Y-%m', REA_DATE)
exercises.reason: Extract the month before grouping and retain the meter identifier.

exercises.title: Unreserved stock lines
exercises.prompt: List part and store combinations in R5STOCK with no matching reservation.
exercises.sql:
SELECT STO_PART,
       STO_STORE
FROM R5STOCK
EXCEPT
SELECT PIP_PART,
       pl.PIC_STORE
FROM R5PICKLISTS pl JOIN R5PICKLISTPARTS pp ON pp.PIP_PICKLIST = pl.PIC_CODE
exercises.reason: EXCEPT compares complete two-column keys.

exercises.title: Parts in both flows
exercises.prompt: Return distinct part codes appearing in both R5ORDERLINES and R5ISSUES.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ORL_PART
FROM R5ORDERLINES INTERSECT
SELECT ISS_PART
FROM R5ISSUES
exercises.reason: INTERSECT returns the keys common to the two sets.

exercises.title: All part demand
exercises.prompt: List distinct part codes found in R5REQUISLINES or R5PICKLISTS / R5PICKLISTPARTS.
exercises.sql:
SELECT RQL_PART
FROM R5REQUISLINES
UNION
SELECT PIP_PART
FROM R5PICKLISTS pl JOIN R5PICKLISTPARTS pp ON pp.PIP_PICKLIST = pl.PIC_CODE
exercises.reason: UNION removes duplicates both within and between inputs.

exercises.title: Signed movement ledger
exercises.prompt: Return part and total signed units using R5DOCKLINES as positive and issues as negative. Recover receipt part from the purchase line.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ORL_PART,
       SUM(delta)
FROM
  (SELECT l.ORL_PART,
          r.DKL_RECVQTY AS delta
   FROM R5DOCKLINES r
   JOIN R5ORDERLINES l ON l.ORL_ORDER=r.DKL_ORDER
   AND l.ORL_ORDLINE=r.DKL_ORDLINE
   UNION ALL SELECT ISS_PART,-ISS_QTY
   FROM R5ISSUES)
GROUP BY ORL_PART
exercises.reason: UNION ALL preserves distinct transactions that happen to carry equal quantities.

exercises.title: Labor value
exercises.prompt: Return work order number and total actual labor value for orders with bookings.
exercises.sql:
SELECT BOO_EVENT,
       SUM(BOO_HOURS*BOO_RATE)
FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS
GROUP BY BOO_EVENT
exercises.reason: Use the rate recorded on each booking before aggregating.

exercises.title: Nominal versus booked rate
exercises.prompt: For each booking return id, recorded rate and nominal trade rate of the employee.
exercises.sql:
SELECT l.BOO_CODE,
       l.BOO_RATE,
       t.TRR_NTRATE
FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS l
JOIN R5PERSONNEL e ON e.PER_CODE=l.BOO_PERSON
JOIN R5TRADERATES t ON t.TRR_TRADE=e.PER_TRADE
exercises.reason: Two joins connect the booking to its assigned trade without rewriting the historical rate.

exercises.title: Material share of cost
exercises.prompt: For orders with issues return order ID and issued value as a percentage of order cost rounded to one decimal. Use NULL for zero cost.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.EVT_CODE,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(m.ISS_QTY*m.ISS_PRICE)/NULLIF(ec.EVO_TOTAL, 0), 1)
FROM R5EVENTS w JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE
JOIN R5ISSUES m ON m.ISS_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE
GROUP BY w.EVT_CODE,
         ec.EVO_TOTAL
exercises.reason: A decimal numerator avoids integer division and NULLIF protects a zero denominator.

exercises.title: Equipment status summary
exercises.prompt: Return each location and the number of distinct assets there with at least one open order. Include R5FACILITIES represented in R5OBJECTS with zero open orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.OBJ_LOCATION,
       COUNT(DISTINCT w.EVT_OBJECT)
FROM R5OBJECTS e
LEFT JOIN R5EVENTS w ON w.EVT_OBJECT=e.OBJ_CODE
AND w.EVT_STATUS='Open'
WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A' GROUP BY e.OBJ_LOCATION
exercises.reason: Put the status test in the join so R5FACILITIES without open orders survive.

exercises.title: Latest inspection ID
exercises.prompt: For every inspected asset return R5OBJECTS code and the result associated with its highest inspection ID.
exercises.sql:
SELECT i.ACK_OBJECT,
       i.ACK_FINDING
FROM R5ACTCHECKLISTS i
WHERE i.ACK_CODE=
    (SELECT MAX(j.ACK_CODE)
     FROM R5ACTCHECKLISTS j
     WHERE j.ACK_OBJECT=i.ACK_OBJECT)
exercises.reason: Find the highest ID for the same asset before retrieving the corresponding result.

exercises.title: Active suppliers without orders
exercises.prompt: List all supplier codes with no purchase order in the dataset.
exercises.sql:
SELECT s.COM_CODE
FROM R5COMPANIES s
LEFT JOIN R5ORDERS p ON p.ORD_SUPPLIER=s.COM_CODE
WHERE p.ORD_CODE IS NULL
exercises.reason: A missing right-side primary key identifies the unmatched supplier.

exercises.title: Approval share
exercises.prompt: For each REQ_ORG appearing in R5REQUISITIONS return REQ_ORG and percentage of R5REQUISITIONS Approved, rounded to one decimal.
exercises.sql:
SELECT REQ_ORG,
       ROUND(100.0*AVG(CASE
                           WHEN REQ_STATUS='Approved' THEN 1
                           ELSE 0
                       END), 1)
FROM R5REQUISITIONS
GROUP BY REQ_ORG
exercises.reason: The average of a zero-or-one indicator is the share of matching records.

exercises.title: Calendar delay
exercises.prompt: For every event dated after 2026-01-01 return AVA_SQLIDENTITY and integer days elapsed since that date.
exercises.sql:
SELECT AVA_SQLIDENTITY,
       CAST(julianday(AVA_CHANGED)-julianday('2026-01-01') AS INTEGER)
FROM R5AUDVALUES
WHERE AVA_CHANGED>'2026-01-01'
exercises.reason: Subtract Julian-day values to measure the interval across month boundaries.

exercises.title: Asset comparison pairs
exercises.prompt: Return each pair of different assets sharing a location as smaller code, larger code. Include each pair once.
exercises.sql:
SELECT a.OBJ_CODE,
       b.OBJ_CODE
FROM R5OBJECTS a
JOIN R5OBJECTS b ON a.OBJ_LOCATION=b.OBJ_LOCATION
AND a.OBJ_CODE<b.OBJ_CODE WHERE a.OBJ_OBTYPE='A'
exercises.reason: The strict ordering excludes self-pairs and reversed duplicates in one condition.

exercises.title: Net available inventory
exercises.prompt: For every R5STOCK row return part, store and quantity less reserved units at that same part and store.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT PIP_PART,
          pl.PIC_STORE,
          SUM(PIP_QTY) n
   FROM R5PICKLISTS pl JOIN R5PICKLISTPARTS pp ON pp.PIP_PICKLIST = pl.PIC_CODE
   GROUP BY PIP_PART,
            pl.PIC_STORE)
SELECT s.STO_PART,
       s.STO_STORE,
       s.STO_QTY-COALESCE(r.n, 0)
FROM R5STOCK s
LEFT JOIN r ON r.PIP_PART=s.STO_PART
AND r.PIC_STORE=s.STO_STORE
exercises.reason: Reduce R5PICKLISTS / R5PICKLISTPARTS to the R5STOCK grain before attaching their total.

exercises.title: Two independent cost streams
exercises.prompt: For every order return id, booked labor value and issued material value. Supply zero for missing streams.
exercises.sql:
WITH l AS
  (SELECT BOO_EVENT,
          SUM(BOO_HOURS*BOO_RATE) n
   FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS
   GROUP BY BOO_EVENT),
     m AS
  (SELECT ISS_EVENT,
          SUM(ISS_QTY*ISS_PRICE) n
   FROM R5ISSUES
   GROUP BY ISS_EVENT)
SELECT w.EVT_CODE,
       COALESCE(l.n, 0),
       COALESCE(m.n, 0)
FROM R5EVENTS w
LEFT JOIN l ON l.BOO_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE
LEFT JOIN m ON m.ISS_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE
exercises.reason: Aggregate each detail stream first. Joining raw bookings to raw issues creates a cross product.

exercises.title: Activity variance
exercises.prompt: Return BOO_EVENT, activity and actual minus planned hours for every planned activity, including work with zero booked time.
exercises.sql:
SELECT a.ACT_EVENT,
       a.ACT_ACT,
       COALESCE(SUM(l.BOO_HOURS), 0)-a.ACT_EST
FROM R5ACTIVITIES a
LEFT JOIN R5BOOKEDHOURS l ON l.BOO_EVENT=a.ACT_EVENT
AND l.BOO_ACT=a.ACT_ACT
GROUP BY a.ACT_EVENT,
         a.ACT_ACT,
         a.ACT_EST
exercises.reason: Both R5PARTS of the activity key are required. An unbooked activity has negative variance.

exercises.title: Cost rank within status
exercises.prompt: Return EVT_CODE, status and dense cost rank within status, highest cost first. Ties share a rank.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVT_CODE,
       EVT_STATUS,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY EVT_STATUS
                         ORDER BY ec.EVO_TOTAL DESC)
FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE
exercises.reason: Partitioning restarts the ranking and dense ranks advance without gaps.

exercises.title: Top two per location
exercises.prompt: Return location, order ID and cost for at most two highest-cost orders per location. Break ties by lower ID.
exercises.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT e.OBJ_LOCATION, w.EVT_CODE, ec.EVO_TOTAL, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY e.OBJ_LOCATION ORDER BY ec.EVO_TOTAL DESC, w.EVT_CODE) n FROM R5EVENTS w JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE JOIN R5OBJECTS e ON e.OBJ_CODE = w.EVT_OBJECT WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE = 'A') SELECT OBJ_LOCATION, EVT_CODE, EVO_TOTAL FROM x WHERE n <= 2
exercises.reason: Assign deterministic positions within each location, then filter in an outer query.

exercises.title: Meter increments
exercises.prompt: Return meter, reading ID and change from its previous REA_READING in date and ID sequence. Keep NULL for the first.
exercises.sql:
SELECT REA_METER,
       REA_CODE,
       REA_READING-LAG(REA_READING) OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER
                                 ORDER BY REA_DATE, REA_CODE)
FROM R5READINGS
exercises.reason: LAG looks at the prior row within the same meter’s sequence.

exercises.title: Running issued value
exercises.prompt: Return issue ID, work order and cumulative issued value within that order in ascending issue ID sequence.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ISS_PK,
       ISS_EVENT,
       SUM(ISS_QTY*ISS_PRICE) OVER(PARTITION BY ISS_EVENT
                                    ORDER BY ISS_PK ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
FROM R5ISSUES
exercises.reason: An explicit row frame includes all earlier issue rows and the current one.

exercises.title: Last three readings
exercises.prompt: Return REA_READING ID and trailing average of up to three readings for the same meter, rounded to two decimals. Order the window by date then ID.
exercises.sql:
SELECT REA_CODE,
       ROUND(AVG(REA_READING) OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER
                               ORDER BY REA_DATE, REA_CODE ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2)
FROM R5READINGS
exercises.reason: ROWS counts observations, so sparse dates still contribute the last three recorded values.

exercises.title: Latest status per order
exercises.prompt: For every order with events return AVA_PRIMARYID, latest AVA_CHANGED and status. Break same-date ties by highest event ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                            ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED DESC, AVA_SQLIDENTITY DESC) n
   FROM R5AUDVALUES)
SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
       AVA_CHANGED,
       AVA_TO
FROM x
WHERE n=1
exercises.reason: A deterministic row number retrieves the whole latest event.

exercises.title: Time to next event
exercises.prompt: Return event ID and the whole days until the next event for the same order, in date and ID sequence. Keep NULL at the end.
exercises.sql:
SELECT AVA_SQLIDENTITY,
       CAST(julianday(LEAD(AVA_CHANGED) OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                                            ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED, AVA_SQLIDENTITY))-julianday(AVA_CHANGED) AS INTEGER)
FROM R5AUDVALUES
exercises.reason: LEAD provides the next date; subtract the current date to measure elapsed days.

exercises.title: First versus current reading
exercises.prompt: Return each reading ID and difference from that meter’s very first reading by date and ID.
exercises.sql:
SELECT REA_CODE,
       REA_READING-FIRST_VALUE(REA_READING) OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER
                                         ORDER BY REA_DATE, REA_CODE)
FROM R5READINGS
exercises.reason: FIRST_VALUE holds the baseline fixed while the current reading advances.

exercises.title: Category contribution
exercises.prompt: Return status and its percentage of total work-order cost rounded to two decimals. Return NULL when the total is zero.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVT_STATUS,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL)/NULLIF(SUM(SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL)) OVER(), 0), 2)
FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE
GROUP BY EVT_STATUS
exercises.reason: Group first; the window sum then acts on group totals.

exercises.title: Above location average
exercises.prompt: Return order id, location and cost for orders strictly above their own location’s average order cost.
exercises.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT w.EVT_CODE, e.OBJ_LOCATION, ec.EVO_TOTAL, AVG(ec.EVO_TOTAL) OVER(PARTITION BY e.OBJ_LOCATION) avg_cost FROM R5EVENTS w JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE JOIN R5OBJECTS e ON e.OBJ_CODE = w.EVT_OBJECT WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE = 'A') SELECT EVT_CODE, OBJ_LOCATION, EVO_TOTAL FROM x WHERE EVO_TOTAL > avg_cost
exercises.reason: A partition average annotates every order without collapsing it into a group.

exercises.title: Maximum-cost ties
exercises.prompt: Return EVT_OBJECT, EVT_CODE and cost for every order tied for highest cost on its own asset.
exercises.sql:
SELECT EVT_OBJECT,
       EVT_CODE,
       ec.EVO_TOTAL
FROM R5EVENTS w JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM R5EVENTS v
     WHERE v.EVT_OBJECT=w.EVT_OBJECT
       AND ec.EVO_TOTAL>ec.EVO_TOTAL)
exercises.reason: A maximum has no strictly larger peer, which retains every tie.

exercises.title: Stores stocking all parts
exercises.prompt: Return store codes stocking every part in the R5PARTS master, regardless of quantity.
exercises.sql:
SELECT s.STR_CODE
FROM R5STORES s
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM R5PARTS p
     WHERE NOT EXISTS
         (SELECT 1
          FROM R5STOCK x
          WHERE x.STO_STORE=s.STR_CODE
            AND x.STO_PART=p.PAR_CODE))
exercises.reason: Double NOT EXISTS expresses that no required part is missing.

exercises.title: Positive outstanding lines
exercises.prompt: For each supplier with purchase lines return supplier and number of lines with a positive unreceived balance, including zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT DKL_ORDER,
          DKL_ORDLINE,
          SUM(DKL_RECVQTY) qty
   FROM R5DOCKLINES
   GROUP BY DKL_ORDER,
            DKL_ORDLINE)
SELECT p.ORD_SUPPLIER,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN l.ORL_ORDQTY>COALESCE(r.qty, 0) THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END)
FROM R5ORDERS p
JOIN R5ORDERLINES l ON l.ORL_ORDER=p.ORD_CODE
LEFT JOIN r ON r.DKL_ORDER=l.ORL_ORDER
AND r.DKL_ORDLINE=l.ORL_ORDLINE
GROUP BY p.ORD_SUPPLIER
exercises.reason: Compute the received amount once per line before counting exceptions.

exercises.title: Current stock coverage
exercises.prompt: For every part in R5STOCK return part and count of R5STORES where on-hand less R5PICKLISTS / R5PICKLISTPARTS meets or exceeds reorder level.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT PIP_PART,
          pl.PIC_STORE,
          SUM(PIP_QTY) q
   FROM R5PICKLISTS pl JOIN R5PICKLISTPARTS pp ON pp.PIP_PICKLIST = pl.PIC_CODE
   GROUP BY PIP_PART,
            pl.PIC_STORE)
SELECT s.STO_PART,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN s.STO_QTY-COALESCE(r.q, 0)>=s.STO_ORDLEV THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END)
FROM R5STOCK s
LEFT JOIN r ON r.PIP_PART=s.STO_PART
AND r.PIC_STORE=s.STO_STORE
GROUP BY s.STO_PART
exercises.reason: Evaluate coverage independently at each store before summing successes.

exercises.title: Receipt-weighted price
exercises.prompt: For each received part return part and average unit price weighted by received units, rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql:
SELECT l.ORL_PART,
       ROUND(SUM(l.ORL_PRICE*r.DKL_RECVQTY)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(r.DKL_RECVQTY), 0), 2)
FROM R5DOCKLINES r
JOIN R5ORDERLINES l ON l.ORL_ORDER=r.DKL_ORDER
AND l.ORL_ORDLINE=r.DKL_ORDLINE
GROUP BY l.ORL_PART
exercises.reason: Weight the agreed line price by units actually received.

exercises.title: Repeated status events
exercises.prompt: List event ID and AVA_PRIMARYID when the event status equals the immediately preceding status for that order in date and ID sequence.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(AVA_TO) OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                           ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED, AVA_SQLIDENTITY) prev
   FROM R5AUDVALUES)
SELECT AVA_SQLIDENTITY,
       AVA_PRIMARYID
FROM x
WHERE AVA_TO=prev
exercises.reason: LAG compares neighboring observations instead of all events with the same status.

exercises.title: Earliest closure
exercises.prompt: For orders with a Closed event return AVA_PRIMARYID, first event date and first Closed event date.
exercises.sql:
SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
       MIN(AVA_CHANGED),
       MIN(CASE
               WHEN AVA_TO='Closed' THEN AVA_CHANGED
           END)
FROM R5AUDVALUES
GROUP BY AVA_PRIMARYID
HAVING COUNT(CASE
                 WHEN AVA_TO='Closed' THEN 1
             END)>0
exercises.reason: Conditional MIN picks the earliest closure while unrestricted MIN retains the true start.

exercises.title: Status transitions
exercises.prompt: Return previous status, new status and number of actual changes across all orders. Ignore first events and unchanged statuses.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT AVA_TO,
          LAG(AVA_TO) OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                           ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED, AVA_SQLIDENTITY) prev
   FROM R5AUDVALUES)
SELECT prev,
       AVA_TO,
       COUNT(*)
FROM x
WHERE prev<>AVA_TO
GROUP BY prev,
         AVA_TO
exercises.reason: First derive neighboring pairs within each order, then pool comparable transitions.

exercises.title: Locations with complete inspection coverage
exercises.prompt: Return R5FACILITIES where every asset has at least one inspection.
exercises.sql:
SELECT OBJ_LOCATION
FROM R5OBJECTS e
GROUP BY OBJ_LOCATION
HAVING COUNT(*)=SUM(CASE
                        WHEN EXISTS
                               (SELECT 1
                                FROM R5ACTCHECKLISTS i
                                WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A' AND i.ACK_OBJECT=e.OBJ_CODE) THEN 1
                        ELSE 0
                    END)
exercises.reason: Compare the asset count with the number of assets having evidence; multiple R5ACTCHECKLISTS still count once.

exercises.title: Monthly milestone
exercises.prompt: For each meter-month return meter, YYYY-MM and its last recorded reading by date then ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          strftime('%Y-%m', REA_DATE) m,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER, strftime('%Y-%m', REA_DATE)
                            ORDER BY REA_DATE DESC, REA_CODE DESC) n
   FROM R5READINGS)
SELECT REA_METER,
       m,
       REA_READING
FROM x
WHERE n=1
exercises.reason: Use the latest observation, even when a reset makes it smaller than an earlier reading.

exercises.title: Project utilization
exercises.prompt: For every project return code, budget and percent of budget represented by its linked work-order costs, rounded to two decimals. Use zero spend for R5PROJECTS without work and NULL for zero budgets.
exercises.sql: SELECT p.PRJ_CODE, p.PRJ_ORIGBUD, ROUND(100.0*COALESCE(SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL), 0)/NULLIF(p.PRJ_ORIGBUD, 0), 2) FROM R5PROJECTS p LEFT JOIN R5EVENTS w ON w.EVT_PROJECT = p.PRJ_CODE LEFT JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE GROUP BY p.PRJ_CODE, p.PRJ_ORIGBUD
exercises.reason: Start from R5PROJECTS so an empty project survives both joins.

exercises.title: Days without events
exercises.prompt: Return every date from 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-10 inclusive on which no order event occurred.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE days(d) AS
  (SELECT '2026-01-01'
   UNION ALL SELECT date(d, '+1 day')
   FROM days
   WHERE d<'2026-01-10')
SELECT d
FROM days
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM R5AUDVALUES e
     WHERE e.AVA_CHANGED=d)
exercises.reason: Generate the complete calendar, then subtract dates with observations.

exercises.title: Compress the event history
exercises.prompt: Return AVA_PRIMARYID, status, first date, last date and event count for each consecutive run of the same status. Sequence each order by event date then ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH a AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(AVA_TO) OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                           ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED, AVA_SQLIDENTITY) prev
   FROM R5AUDVALUES),
     b AS
  (SELECT *,
          SUM(CASE
                  WHEN AVA_TO=prev THEN 0
                  ELSE 1
              END) OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                        ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED, AVA_SQLIDENTITY) grp
   FROM a)
SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
       AVA_TO,
       MIN(AVA_CHANGED),
       MAX(AVA_CHANGED),
       COUNT(*)
FROM b
GROUP BY AVA_PRIMARYID,
         grp,
         AVA_TO
exercises.reason: Mark the first row of each run, cumulatively number the marks and aggregate within each run.

exercises.title: Longest daily streak
exercises.prompt: For each order with events return AVA_PRIMARYID and the length of its longest streak of consecutive distinct event dates.
exercises.sql:
WITH d AS
  (SELECT DISTINCT AVA_PRIMARYID,
                   AVA_CHANGED
   FROM R5AUDVALUES),
     g AS
  (SELECT *,
          julianday(AVA_CHANGED)-ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                                                  ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED) k
   FROM d),
     n AS
  (SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
          k,
          COUNT(*) LEN
   FROM g
   GROUP BY AVA_PRIMARYID,
            k)
SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
       MAX(LEN)
FROM n
GROUP BY AVA_PRIMARYID
exercises.reason: Deduplicate dates before subtracting row number from day number. Consecutive days share an island key.

exercises.title: Reopening after closure
exercises.prompt: For each change from Closed to Open return AVA_PRIMARYID, reopening ID and integer days since the immediately preceding Closed event. Use date then ID sequence.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(AVA_TO) OVER w prev,
          LAG(AVA_CHANGED) OVER w prev_date
   FROM R5AUDVALUES WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                                  ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED,
                                           AVA_SQLIDENTITY))
SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
       AVA_SQLIDENTITY,
       CAST(julianday(AVA_CHANGED)-julianday(prev_date) AS INTEGER)
FROM x
WHERE AVA_TO='Open'
  AND prev='Closed'
exercises.reason: Calculate both previous values before filtering so the closure remains in the window.

exercises.title: As-of snapshot
exercises.prompt: Return each work order’s ID and last event status on or before 2026-01-05. Use NULL if unknown, and highest ID to break same-day ties.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.EVT_CODE,
  (SELECT e.AVA_TO
   FROM R5AUDVALUES e
   WHERE e.AVA_PRIMARYID=w.EVT_CODE
     AND e.AVA_CHANGED<='2026-01-05'
   ORDER BY e.AVA_CHANGED DESC,
            e.AVA_SQLIDENTITY DESC
   LIMIT 1)
FROM R5EVENTS w
exercises.reason: Restrict history to the cutoff before selecting its latest event. Drive the result from all orders.

exercises.title: Daily open backlog
exercises.prompt: For each date from 2026-01-01 through 2026-01-10 return date and count of work orders whose latest known status by that day’s end was Open. Highest ID wins date ties. Exclude unknown states from the count.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(DAY) AS
  (SELECT '2026-01-01'
   UNION ALL SELECT date(DAY, '+1 day')
   FROM d
   WHERE DAY<'2026-01-10')
SELECT DAY,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM R5EVENTS w
   WHERE
       (SELECT AVA_TO
        FROM R5AUDVALUES e
        WHERE e.AVA_PRIMARYID=w.EVT_CODE
          AND e.AVA_CHANGED<=d.day
        ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED DESC,
                 AVA_SQLIDENTITY DESC
        LIMIT 1)='Open')
FROM d
exercises.reason: Generate reporting days and carry forward the most recent state separately for each order.

exercises.title: Time spent open
exercises.prompt: Return AVA_PRIMARYID and whole days in Open status across event intervals for every order with events. Close the final interval at 2026-02-01. Use date then ID sequence; same-day intervals contribute zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LEAD(AVA_CHANGED, 1, '2026-02-01') OVER(PARTITION BY AVA_PRIMARYID
                                                 ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED, AVA_SQLIDENTITY) STOP
   FROM R5AUDVALUES)
SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
       CAST(SUM(CASE
                    WHEN AVA_TO='Open' THEN julianday(STOP)-julianday(AVA_CHANGED)
                    ELSE 0
                END) AS INTEGER)
FROM x
GROUP BY AVA_PRIMARYID
exercises.reason: An event establishes status until the next event. Sum durations only for the intervals beginning open.

exercises.title: Median order cost
exercises.prompt: Return status and median order cost per status, averaging the two middle costs when the count is even.
exercises.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT e.EVT_STATUS, ec.EVO_TOTAL, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY e.EVT_STATUS ORDER BY ec.EVO_TOTAL, e.EVT_CODE) n, COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY e.EVT_STATUS) cnt FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE) SELECT EVT_STATUS, AVG(EVO_TOTAL) FROM x WHERE n IN ((cnt+1)/2, (cnt+2)/2) GROUP BY EVT_STATUS
exercises.reason: SQLite integer division yields the middle positions for odd and even groups.

exercises.title: Pareto cutoff
exercises.prompt: Return R5OBJECTS code and total cost for the smallest prefix of assets with work that reaches at least 80 percent of total cost. Sort by descending asset total then code to resolve ties. Assume positive overall cost.
exercises.sql:
WITH a AS
  (SELECT EVT_OBJECT,
          SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL) v
   FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE
   GROUP BY EVT_OBJECT),
     b AS
  (SELECT *,
          SUM(v) OVER(
                      ORDER BY v DESC, EVT_OBJECT) running,
                 SUM(v) OVER() total
   FROM a)
SELECT EVT_OBJECT,
       v
FROM b
WHERE running-v<0.8*total
exercises.reason: Test the total before adding the current asset. This includes the asset that crosses the threshold.

exercises.title: Exclude the current order
exercises.prompt: For orders having another order on the same asset, return ID and average cost of all other orders on that asset rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT e.EVT_CODE, ec.EVO_TOTAL, SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL) OVER(PARTITION BY e.EVT_OBJECT) total, COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY e.EVT_OBJECT) n FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE) SELECT EVT_CODE, ROUND((total-EVO_TOTAL)*1.0/(n-1), 2) FROM x WHERE n>1
exercises.reason: Remove one value and one observation from the partition totals; singletons have no comparison.

exercises.title: Meter reset correction
exercises.prompt: For every meter return meter and accumulated usage across successive readings. A decrease indicates a reset to zero; count the new reading as the usage since reset. The first reading contributes zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(REA_READING) OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER
                            ORDER BY REA_DATE, REA_CODE) prev
   FROM R5READINGS)
SELECT REA_METER,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN prev IS NULL THEN 0
               WHEN REA_READING<prev THEN REA_READING
               ELSE REA_READING-prev
           END)
FROM x
GROUP BY REA_METER
exercises.reason: Handle baseline, reset and normal increment separately before summing.

exercises.title: Peak daily consumption
exercises.prompt: For each meter return meter, ending reading ID and highest usage per elapsed day rounded to two decimals. Use successive observations ordered by date then ID. Ignore resets and zero-day intervals. Resolve equal rates by smaller ending ID; omit R5METERS without eligible intervals.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(REA_READING) OVER w pv,
          LAG(REA_DATE) OVER w pd
   FROM R5READINGS WINDOW w AS(PARTITION BY REA_METER
                                   ORDER BY REA_DATE,
                                            REA_CODE)),
     y AS
  (SELECT *,
          (REA_READING-pv)/(julianday(REA_DATE)-julianday(pd)) rate
   FROM x
   WHERE REA_READING>=pv
     AND REA_DATE>pd),
     z AS
  (SELECT *,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER
                            ORDER BY rate DESC, REA_CODE) n
   FROM y)
SELECT REA_METER,
       REA_CODE,
       ROUND(rate, 2)
FROM z
WHERE n=1
exercises.reason: Rank unrounded rates after eliminating intervals with invalid duration or reset behavior.

exercises.title: Seven-day event volume
exercises.prompt: For each observed event date return date and number of events in the inclusive seven-calendar-day window ending that day.
exercises.sql:
WITH d AS
  (SELECT AVA_CHANGED,
          COUNT(*) n
   FROM R5AUDVALUES
   GROUP BY AVA_CHANGED)
SELECT AVA_CHANGED,
       SUM(n) OVER(
                   ORDER BY julianday(AVA_CHANGED) RANGE BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
FROM d
exercises.reason: RANGE operates on elapsed days; seven prior result rows could span far more than a week.

exercises.title: Cumulative unique orders
exercises.prompt: For each observed event date return date and number of distinct work orders observed up to and including that date.
exercises.sql:
WITH first_seen AS
  (SELECT AVA_PRIMARYID,
          MIN(AVA_CHANGED) first_day
   FROM R5AUDVALUES
   GROUP BY AVA_PRIMARYID),
     days AS
  (SELECT DISTINCT AVA_CHANGED
   FROM R5AUDVALUES)
SELECT AVA_CHANGED,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM first_seen
   WHERE first_day<=days.AVA_CHANGED)
FROM days
exercises.reason: Each order enters the cumulative population just once on its first date.

exercises.title: Depth of descendants
exercises.prompt: Starting at COOL-SYS, return every distinct reachable child and its minimum positive edge count. The training hierarchy is acyclic.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x(node, depth) AS
  (SELECT STC_CHILD,
          1
   FROM R5STRUCTURES
   WHERE STC_PARENT='COOL-SYS'
   UNION ALL SELECT l.STC_CHILD,
                    x.depth+1
   FROM x
   JOIN R5STRUCTURES l ON l.STC_PARENT=x.node)
SELECT node,
       MIN(depth)
FROM x
GROUP BY node
exercises.reason: Walk down child links and keep the shortest path when a node is reachable by several routes.

exercises.title: Roll costs up the hierarchy
exercises.prompt: Return one total cost across work orders on all descendants of COOL-SYS. Count each descendant’s orders once, even if two paths reach it. Exclude the root.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x(node) AS
  (SELECT STC_CHILD
   FROM R5STRUCTURES
   WHERE STC_PARENT='COOL-SYS'
   UNION SELECT l.STC_CHILD
   FROM R5STRUCTURES l
   JOIN x ON l.STC_PARENT=x.node)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL), 0)
FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE
WHERE EVT_OBJECT IN
    (SELECT node
     FROM x)
exercises.reason: UNION collapses duplicate node identities before the financial aggregation.

exercises.title: Find terminal descendants
exercises.prompt: Return distinct descendants reachable from COOL-SYS that have no children of their own.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x(node) AS
  (SELECT STC_CHILD
   FROM R5STRUCTURES
   WHERE STC_PARENT='COOL-SYS'
   UNION SELECT l.STC_CHILD
   FROM R5STRUCTURES l
   JOIN x ON l.STC_PARENT=x.node)
SELECT node
FROM x
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM R5STRUCTURES l
     WHERE l.STC_PARENT=x.node)
exercises.reason: Traverse first; a reachable node is a leaf when no edge starts there.

exercises.title: Fulfillment classification
exercises.prompt: For every purchase order with lines return ID and class: Over if any line is over-received, Complete if every line exactly matches, None if total R5DOCKLINES are zero, otherwise Partial. Apply rules in this order.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT DKL_ORDER,
          DKL_ORDLINE,
          SUM(DKL_RECVQTY) q
   FROM R5DOCKLINES
   GROUP BY DKL_ORDER,
            DKL_ORDLINE),
     a AS
  (SELECT l.ORL_ORDER,
          l.ORL_ORDQTY,
          COALESCE(r.q, 0) q
   FROM R5ORDERLINES l
   LEFT JOIN r ON r.DKL_ORDER=l.ORL_ORDER
   AND r.DKL_ORDLINE=l.ORL_ORDLINE)
SELECT ORL_ORDER,
       CASE
           WHEN MAX(q>ORL_ORDQTY)=1 THEN 'Over'
           WHEN MIN(q=ORL_ORDQTY)=1 THEN 'Complete'
           WHEN SUM(q)=0 THEN 'None'
           ELSE 'Partial'
       END
FROM a
GROUP BY ORL_ORDER
exercises.reason: Compare at line level before classifying an order. Over-delivery on one line cannot cancel a shortage on another.

exercises.title: FIFO reservation allocation
exercises.prompt: For each reservation return ID and units that can be filled from its part-store on-hand R5STOCK. Allocate to smaller reservation IDs first. Missing R5STOCK means zero and partial allocation is allowed.
exercises.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT pl.PIC_CODE, pl.PIC_STORE, pp.PIP_PART, pp.PIP_QTY, SUM(pp.PIP_QTY) OVER(PARTITION BY pp.PIP_PART, pl.PIC_STORE ORDER BY pl.PIC_CODE ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) - pp.PIP_QTY AS prior FROM R5PICKLISTS pl JOIN R5PICKLISTPARTS pp ON pp.PIP_PICKLIST = pl.PIC_CODE) SELECT x.PIC_CODE, MAX(0, MIN(x.PIP_QTY, COALESCE(s.STO_QTY, 0) - x.prior)) FROM x LEFT JOIN R5STOCK s ON s.STO_PART = x.PIP_PART AND s.STO_STORE = x.PIC_STORE
exercises.reason: Subtract earlier demand from starting R5STOCK, then clamp the available amount between zero and this request.

exercises.title: Move stock between stores
exercises.prompt: For every ordered pair of different R5STORES stocking the same part, return part, donor, recipient and transferable units only when positive. Keep the donor at its reorder level and cap the transfer at the recipient’s shortage. Evaluate pairs independently.
exercises.sql:
SELECT d.STO_PART,
       d.STO_STORE,
       r.STO_STORE,
       MIN(d.STO_QTY-d.STO_ORDLEV, r.STO_ORDLEV-r.STO_QTY)
FROM R5STOCK d
JOIN R5STOCK r ON d.STO_PART=r.STO_PART
AND d.STO_STORE<>r.STO_STORE
WHERE d.STO_QTY>d.STO_ORDLEV
  AND r.STO_QTY<r.STO_ORDLEV
exercises.reason: A valid pair needs both a surplus and a shortage. The smaller quantity limits its independent transfer.

exercises.title: Allocate shared project cost
exercises.prompt: Split each linked work order’s cost equally across its linked R5PROJECTS. Return every project code and allocated cost rounded to two decimals, including zero.
exercises.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT w.EVT_PROJECT, ec.EVO_TOTAL * 1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY w.EVT_CODE) AS share FROM R5EVENTS w JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE WHERE w.EVT_PROJECT IS NOT NULL) SELECT p.PRJ_CODE, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(a.share), 0), 2) FROM R5PROJECTS p LEFT JOIN a ON a.EVT_PROJECT = p.PRJ_CODE GROUP BY p.PRJ_CODE
exercises.reason: Divide at work-order grain before summing shares by project to conserve total cost.

exercises.title: Largest cost component
exercises.prompt: For each work order return id and largest of Labor, Material and Other. Other equals order cost less booked labor and issued material. Break ties in the listed order. Missing detail totals are zero.
exercises.sql: WITH l AS (SELECT BOO_EVENT, SUM(BOO_HOURS*BOO_RATE) v FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS GROUP BY BOO_EVENT), m AS (SELECT ISS_EVENT, SUM(ISS_QTY*ISS_PRICE) v FROM R5ISSUES GROUP BY ISS_EVENT), a AS (SELECT w.EVT_CODE, ec.EVO_TOTAL, COALESCE(l.v, 0) labor, COALESCE(m.v, 0) mat FROM R5EVENTS w JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE LEFT JOIN l ON l.BOO_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE LEFT JOIN m ON m.ISS_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE) SELECT EVT_CODE, CASE WHEN labor>=mat AND labor>=EVO_TOTAL-labor-mat THEN 'Labor' WHEN mat>=EVO_TOTAL-labor-mat THEN 'Material' ELSE 'Other' END FROM a
exercises.reason: Reconcile independent detail totals first. The order of CASE conditions implements the tie rule.

exercises.title: First crossing of budget
exercises.prompt: For R5PROJECTS with a crossing, return project code and first work-order ID where cumulative linked order costs in ID order strictly exceed budget. Use full cost per linked order.
exercises.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT p.PRJ_CODE, p.PRJ_ORIGBUD, w.EVT_CODE, SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL) OVER(PARTITION BY p.PRJ_CODE ORDER BY w.EVT_CODE) total FROM R5PROJECTS p JOIN R5EVENTS w ON w.EVT_PROJECT = p.PRJ_CODE JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = w.EVT_CODE) SELECT PRJ_CODE, MIN(EVT_CODE) FROM a WHERE total > PRJ_ORIGBUD GROUP BY PRJ_CODE
exercises.reason: Window the ordered costs per project before locating the first qualifying order.

exercises.title: Matched parts never fully supplied
exercises.prompt: Return distinct part codes that have purchase lines and for which every purchase line has received strictly fewer units than ordered.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT DKL_ORDER,
          DKL_ORDLINE,
          SUM(DKL_RECVQTY) q
   FROM R5DOCKLINES
   GROUP BY DKL_ORDER,
            DKL_ORDLINE),
     a AS
  (SELECT l.ORL_PART,
          l.ORL_ORDQTY,
          COALESCE(r.q, 0) received
   FROM R5ORDERLINES l
   LEFT JOIN r ON l.ORL_ORDER=r.DKL_ORDER
   AND l.ORL_ORDLINE=r.DKL_ORDLINE)
SELECT ORL_PART
FROM a
GROUP BY ORL_PART
HAVING MAX(received>=ORL_ORDQTY)=0
exercises.reason: Express the universal rule by ruling out any complete or over-received line.

exercises.title: Status at inspection dates
exercises.prompt: For each dated inspection in R5ACTCHECKLISTS return visit id and count of orders on that R5OBJECTS whose latest event status by visit day was Open. Highest event ID breaks date ties.
exercises.sql:
SELECT v.ACK_CODE,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM R5EVENTS w
   WHERE w.EVT_OBJECT=v.ACK_OBJECT
     AND
       (SELECT AVA_TO
        FROM R5AUDVALUES e
        WHERE e.AVA_PRIMARYID=w.EVT_CODE
          AND e.AVA_CHANGED<=v.ACK_UPDATED
        ORDER BY AVA_CHANGED DESC,
                 AVA_SQLIDENTITY DESC
        LIMIT 1)='Open')
FROM R5ACTCHECKLISTS v
exercises.reason: Correlate on both the asset and the visit cutoff; current order status can differ from historical status.

exercises.title: Reconcile three reporting grains
exercises.prompt: For each R5OBJECTS location return location, distinct asset count, open order count and booked labor value on open orders. Include R5FACILITIES with no open work. Return zero for missing measures.
exercises.sql: WITH l AS (SELECT BOO_EVENT, SUM(BOO_HOURS*BOO_RATE) v FROM R5BOOKEDHOURS GROUP BY BOO_EVENT), a AS (SELECT w.EVT_OBJECT, COUNT(*) n, SUM(COALESCE(l.v, 0)) v FROM R5EVENTS w LEFT JOIN l ON l.BOO_EVENT=w.EVT_CODE WHERE w.EVT_STATUS='Open' GROUP BY w.EVT_OBJECT) SELECT e.OBJ_LOCATION, COUNT(*), SUM(COALESCE(a.n, 0)), SUM(COALESCE(a.v, 0)) FROM R5OBJECTS e LEFT JOIN a ON a.EVT_OBJECT=e.OBJ_CODE WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A' GROUP BY e.OBJ_LOCATION
exercises.reason: Reduce labor to orders, then orders to assets. The final location group can safely add the measures without multiplying assets.

exercises.title: Asset locations
exercises.prompt: List OBJ_LOCATION and asset code ordered by OBJ_LOCATION then code.
exercises.sql: SELECT OBJ_LOCATION, OBJ_CODE FROM R5OBJECTS WHERE OBJ_OBTYPE='A' ORDER BY OBJ_LOCATION, OBJ_CODE
exercises.reason: Use both requested sort keys.

exercises.title: PM interval register
exercises.prompt: Show basis, interval and schedule code ordered by PPO_PPM.
exercises.sql: SELECT PPO_ISSTYPE, PPO_FREQ, PPO_PPM FROM R5PPMOBJECTS ORDER BY PPO_PPM
exercises.reason: Read intervals together with their units.

exercises.title: Stock buffers
exercises.prompt: Show store, part and STO_QTY above reorder level, sorted by store and part.
exercises.sql: SELECT STO_STORE, STO_PART, STO_QTY-STO_ORDLEV FROM R5STOCK ORDER BY STO_STORE, STO_PART
exercises.reason: Subtract the threshold even when the result is negative.

exercises.title: Order cost range
exercises.prompt: Show status, lowest cost and highest cost by status, sorted by status.
exercises.sql: SELECT EVT_STATUS, MIN(ec.EVO_TOTAL), MAX(ec.EVO_TOTAL) FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE GROUP BY EVT_STATUS ORDER BY EVT_STATUS
exercises.reason: Group by the workflow status.

exercises.title: Meter coverage
exercises.prompt: Show each meter code and number of readings, including empty R5METERS, ordered by code.
exercises.sql: SELECT m.MET_CODE, COUNT(r.REA_CODE) FROM R5METERS m LEFT JOIN R5READINGS r ON r.REA_METER=m.MET_CODE GROUP BY m.MET_CODE ORDER BY m.MET_CODE
exercises.reason: Count the nullable reading identifier.

exercises.title: PM coverage by asset
exercises.prompt: Show asset code and number of associated schedules for every asset ordered by code.
exercises.sql: SELECT e.OBJ_CODE, COUNT(p.PPO_PPM) FROM R5OBJECTS e LEFT JOIN R5PPMOBJECTS p ON p.PPO_OBJECT=e.OBJ_CODE WHERE e.OBJ_OBTYPE='A' GROUP BY e.OBJ_CODE ORDER BY e.OBJ_CODE
exercises.reason: Preserve R5OBJECTS with no schedule.

exercises.title: Latest meter sample
exercises.prompt: Return meter, date and REA_READING for the most recent sample per meter. Break date ties by greatest ID and sort by meter.
exercises.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY REA_METER ORDER BY REA_DATE DESC,REA_CODE DESC) AS n FROM R5READINGS) SELECT REA_METER,REA_DATE,REA_READING FROM ranked WHERE n=1 ORDER BY REA_METER
exercises.reason: Rank readings inside each meter.

exercises.title: Failure-code tally
exercises.prompt: A shift log contains LEAK, SEIZE and LEAK. Use a VALUES CTE to return failure code and incident count ordered by count descending then code. This log is supplied in the prompt.
exercises.sql: WITH log(code) AS (VALUES ('LEAK'),('SEIZE'),('LEAK')) SELECT code,COUNT(*) FROM log GROUP BY code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC,code
exercises.reason: Group the three supplied incidents by code.

exercises.title: Unissued reservations
exercises.prompt: Return distinct work order, part and store for R5PICKLISTS / R5PICKLISTPARTS with no matching material issue on all three keys. Sort by those keys.
exercises.sql: SELECT DISTINCT pl.PIC_EVENT, pp.PIP_PART, pl.PIC_STORE FROM R5PICKLISTS pl JOIN R5PICKLISTPARTS pp ON pp.PIP_PICKLIST = pl.PIC_CODE WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM R5ISSUES i WHERE i.ISS_EVENT = pl.PIC_EVENT AND i.ISS_PART = pp.PIP_PART AND i.ISS_STORE = pl.PIC_STORE) ORDER BY pl.PIC_EVENT, pp.PIP_PART, pl.PIC_STORE
exercises.reason: Test absence using the full reservation context.

exercises.title: Cumulative asset cost
exercises.prompt: For each order return asset, order ID and cumulative cost for that asset through that ID. Sort by asset then ID.
exercises.sql: SELECT EVT_OBJECT,EVT_CODE,SUM(ec.EVO_TOTAL) OVER(PARTITION BY EVT_OBJECT ORDER BY EVT_CODE ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) FROM R5EVENTS e JOIN R5EVENTCOST ec ON ec.EVO_EVENT = e.EVT_CODE ORDER BY EVT_OBJECT,EVT_CODE
exercises.reason: Partition by asset and order the window by order ID.
